subtopics.title: Simplify algebraic fractions
subtopics.exposition: To simplify an algebraic fraction, apply the different factorisation methods to factorise the numerator and the denominator before simplifying the expression. For (x^2 + 3x)/(x + 3), factorising the numerator gives x(x + 3)/(x + 3), and cancelling the common factor (x + 3) leaves x. Use grouping to factorise the numerator and take out the common factor in the denominator: (ax - ab) + (x - b) becomes a(x - b) + (x - b), and ax^2 - abx becomes ax(x - b). After grouping, take out the common factor (x - b) in the numerator: a(x - b) + (x - b) = (x - b)(a + 1). Cancel the common factor (x - b) in the numerator and the denominator to give the final answer (a + 1)/(ax).

subtopics.title: Multiply and divide fractions
subtopics.exposition: Multiplying fractions: a/b x c/d = ac/bd, with b not equal to 0 and d not equal to 0. Dividing fractions: a/b divided by c/d = a/b x d/c = ad/bc, with b, c and d each not equal to 0. Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by the reciprocal of the fraction. To simplify a quotient of algebraic fractions, first factorise the numerator and denominator of each fraction: (x^2 - x - 2)/(x^2 - 4) becomes (x + 1)(x - 2)/((x + 2)(x - 2)), and (x^2 + x)/(x^2 + 2x) becomes x(x + 1)/(x(x + 2)). Change the division sign and multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction: the divisor x(x + 1)/(x(x + 2)) is turned over to give x(x + 2)/(x(x + 1)). After multiplying by the reciprocal, the product of the factorised fractions is written as its final answer, which in this example is 1.

subtopics.title: Add and subtract fractions
subtopics.exposition: For the denominators (x + 2)(x - 2), x - 2 and (x + 2)(x - 2), the lowest common denominator is (x - 2)(x + 2). Adding fractions with the same denominator: a/b + c/b = (a + c)/b, with b not equal to 0. To add or subtract algebraic fractions, first factorise the denominators: x^2 - 4 becomes (x + 2)(x - 2) in the first and third fractions, while the second denominator is x - 2. Make all denominators the same so that the fractions can be added or subtracted. Write each fraction over the lowest common denominator: the fraction x^2/(x - 2) is rewritten as (x^2)(x + 2)/((x + 2)(x - 2)). Write the fractions as one fraction over the common denominator, putting the numerator of the subtracted fraction in brackets: (x - 2 + (x^2)(x + 2) - (x^3 + x - 4)) / ((x + 2)(x - 2)). Simplify the single fraction by simplifying its numerator: x - 2 + x^3 + 2x^2 - x^3 - x + 4 gives 2x^2 + 2, so the fraction is (2x^2 + 2)/((x + 2)(x - 2)). Take out the common factor in the numerator and write the final answer: 2(x^2 + 1)/((x + 2)(x - 2)). In worked example 21 the denominators are factorised first: x^2 - x becomes x(x - 1), x^3 - 1 becomes (x - 1)(x^2 + x + 1), and x^2 - 1 becomes (x - 1)(x + 1). Simplify and find the common denominator, which here is x(x - 1)(x + 1), giving the single fraction (2(x + 1) + x(x + 1) - x^2) / (x(x - 1)(x + 1)). Expand and simplify the numerator to write the final answer: 2x + 2 + x^2 + x - x^2 gives 3x + 2, so the result is (3x + 2)/(x(x - 1)(x + 1)).

subtopics.title: State fraction restrictions
subtopics.exposition: If x = -3 then the denominator x + 3 equals 0 and the fraction (x^2 + 3x)/(x + 3) is undefined. In the product identity a/b x c/d = ac/bd the restrictions are b not equal to 0 and d not equal to 0. In the sum identity a/b + c/b = (a + c)/b the restriction is b not equal to 0. In the quotient identity a/b divided by c/d = ad/bc the restrictions are b not equal to 0, c not equal to 0 and d not equal to 0. The restriction on the variable is written beside the simplified answer in brackets; for (x^2 + 3x)/(x + 3) = x the restriction is written x not equal to -3. For the fraction in worked example 18 the restrictions given are x not equal to 0 and x not equal to b. For the quotient in worked example 19 the restrictions given are x not equal to 0 and x not equal to plus or minus 2. For the sum and difference in worked example 20 the restriction given is x not equal to plus or minus 2. For the sum and difference in worked example 21 the restrictions given are x not equal to 0 and x not equal to plus or minus 1.

Use grouping to factorise the numerator and take out the common factor in the denominator: (ax - ab) + (x - b) becomes a(x - b) + (x - b), and ax^2 - abx becomes ax(x - b).

Change the division sign and multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction: the divisor x(x + 1)/(x(x + 2)) is turned over to give x(x + 2)/(x(x + 1)).
After multiplying by the reciprocal, the product of the factorised fractions is written as its final answer, which in this example is 1.

To add or subtract algebraic fractions, first factorise the denominators: x^2 - 4 becomes (x + 2)(x - 2) in the first and third fractions, while the second denominator is x - 2.
Make all denominators the same so that the fractions can be added or subtracted.
For the denominators (x + 2)(x - 2), x - 2 and (x + 2)(x - 2), the lowest common denominator is (x - 2)(x + 2).

In worked example 21 the denominators are factorised first: x^2 - x becomes x(x - 1), x^3 - 1 becomes (x - 1)(x^2 + x + 1), and x^2 - 1 becomes (x - 1)(x + 1).
